article_title: React Router 8.5.0 Deprecates Its View Transition APIs in Favor of React's ViewTransition Component and Adds an Unstable API-only Mode

content_preview.title: React Router 8.5.0 Deprecates Its View Transition APIs in Favor of React's ViewTransition Component and Adds an Unstable API-only Mode
content_preview.summary: React Router 8.5.0, dated October 19, 2026, deprecates its view transition APIs for React's ViewTransition and adds unstable API-only Mode, custom fetch and route discovery.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

React Router 8.5.0 was published on October 19, 2026, according to the project's [release tag on GitHub](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/releases/tag/react-router@8.5.0), whose notes point to the changelog. The [changelog entry for v8.5.0](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v850) is dated 2026-10-19 and leads with a deprecation of the library's view transition APIs, followed by three features marked unstable: an API-only mode for Framework Mod...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News release report (677 words by the script, within 400-1200). Overview, deprecation, three unstable features, fixes, and a What We Don't Know section. Appropriate technical depth for a developer audience.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources are first-party (React Router project on github.com; React team on react.dev). github.com (line 1131) and react.dev (line 2802) are on config/source_allowlist.txt by exact hostname. No independent third-party sources; documented. Snapshots read: source-0.html.gz (GitHub release page) is a JS-rendered shell whose visible text only shows 'Release v8.5.0 ... react-router@8.5.0 v8.5.0 Latest'; the release date and body were verified via the GitHub API instead: tag react-router@8.5.0, name v8.5.0, published_at 2026-10-19T13:48:57Z, not draft/prerelease, body 'See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v850' (matches the article's 'notes point to the changelog'). source-1.html.gz (CHANGELOG, 627195 bytes) contains the v8.5.0 section ('## v8.5.0', 'Date: 2026-10-19', 'available in React 19.3+', 'unstable_api-only', 'will be removed in v9'); I then re-fetched the raw CHANGELOG.md from raw.githubusercontent.com and verified every claim against the raw v8.5.0 section (lines 123-275, before '## v8.4.0'). VERIFIED against raw text: (1) Deprecation quote verbatim: 'React Router's view transition APIs are now marked deprecated in favor of React's <ViewTransition> component, available in React 19.3+.' The changelog DOES tie the replacement to React 19.3 (19.3+; Minor Changes: 'available in React 19.3 and later'). (2) Deprecated names exactly as listed: viewTransition props/options, useViewTransitionState, NavLink's isTransitioning render prop and transitioning class (changelog also says '.transitioning styles'). Quote 'will continue to work for the duration of React Router v8 and will be removed in v9' verbatim; 'Preserve existing behavior, including support for older React versions' matches. (3) Migration: wrap <ViewTransition> around <Outlet> in a persistent layout, remove viewTransition props/options, replace useViewTransitionState/isTransitioning/.transitioning with React's View Transition classes, do not set useTransitions={false}: all match. (4) Three unstable features, all under the 8.5.0 heading (not 8.4.x; v8.4.0 begins at line 276) and each labelled '(unstable)' in headings and listed under '### Unstable Changes' with the warning 'Unstable features are not recommended for production use': API-only Mode (ssr: "unstable_api-only" in react-router.config.ts, optional prerender list, unstable_apiServerOrigin, CORS and allowedActionOrigins); Custom Fetch (unstable_fetch on <HydratedRouter>, context types initialization/navigation/fetcher/revalidation/manifest, navigationType PUSH/REPLACE/POP, uses list, return bodies unchanged for manifest and Turbo Stream protocols, <Link prefetch> uses native link rel=prefetch and does not call the custom implementation); Application-Controlled Route Discovery (future.unstable_customRouteDiscovery, unstable_useRouteDiscovery, discoverRoutes(paths), loadAllRoutes(), state partial/loading/complete, quote 'loads route metadata without navigating, running loaders/actions, or prefetching route modules' verbatim, onManifestMismatch behavior): all match. Quote 'Framework Mode can now serve static HTML while retaining a runtime server for loaders, actions, revalidation, and lazy route discovery' verbatim. (5) Fixes section: optional peer deps for @types/react and @types/react-dom, matchPath static segment outside [\w-], fetcher.reset() revalidation, @react-router/node temp-file-and-rename session write, @react-router/express IPv6 Host/X-Forwarded-Host port: all match (PR numbers, which the article does not cite, not checked further). No contributor credits are named in the changelog entries, and the article names none. (6) source-2.html.gz (react.dev ViewTransition reference, snapshot and live raw re-fetch, both 37540 chars of text): '<ViewTransition> lets you animate a component tree with Transitions and Suspense.' verbatim in both; no differences found between snapshot and live. The react.dev page carries a v19.3 header, but it does not itself say 'stable' (the page has no 'Canary' banner); the article attributes only the description sentence to this page, and the 'stabilized in React 19.3' statement is attributed to The Machine Herald's earlier report, not to react.dev. (7) Internal link /article/2026-10/06-react-193-makes-viewtransition-and-fragment-refs-stable-adds-usebrowser-and-trusted-types-support resolves to an existing published article (src/content/articles/2026-10/06-react-193-...-support.md, same slug); it is accurately described: that article's title and summary say React 19.3 (Sept 9, 2026) stabilizes ViewTransition. This is consistent with the React Router changelog's 'available in React 19.3+' and with the v19.3 react.dev page. Snapshots flagged by suspicious_patterns scan: none (all null); no instruction-like text addressed to an AI found. Orphan-link check: all body URLs (github release tag, changelog #v850, react.dev reference) are in article.sources; the only other link is the internal Herald path.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, name, config key, date and quote checked against raw text and API. Release date October 19, 2026 confirmed by API published_at and changelog 'Date: 2026-10-19'. Minor imprecision (not requiring correction): the article says the changelog 'leads with' the deprecation and lists the three features as 'marked unstable'; in the changelog they appear as '(unstable)' sections plus an 'Unstable Changes' list. The summary says 'custom fetch and route discovery' which is a fair shortening.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Herald coverage of React Router (only an unrelated npm-worm article mentions it); it builds on the earlier React 19.3 article via an accurate internal link and a different angle (downstream framework adoption).
concerns: All three sources are first-party (React Router project and React team); no independent third-party coverage. Acceptable for a release-notes News piece and attributed throughout.
The GitHub release page snapshot is a JS-rendered shell with little text; the release body was verified through the GitHub API.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed release coverage with all quotes verbatim and all claims traceable to the v8.5.0 changelog section; ready for publication. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid release coverage of a deprecation and unstable features for React Router developers, not broad-audience news
